explanation: The March 15, 2017 document contains a rate hike (fed funds target raised to 3/4–1 percent) and substantive forward guidance on balance sheet normalization, with most participants anticipating reinvestment changes 'later this year' — a materially earlier timeline than markets had priced. These two signals together (the hike itself plus the accelerated balance sheet discussion) plausibly explain a structural break around March 21, as markets digested the full minutes detail on balance sheet normalization timing that was not fully conveyed in the initial post-meeting statement.
